sections.h2: Who values and who collects property tax in Richland County, Ohio?
sections.html:
The county auditor sets the value of every parcel, and the county treasurer mails the bills and takes the payments. Both offices sit at 50 Park Avenue East in Mansfield, Ohio 44902, with weekday hours of 8am to 4pm. The auditor's number is 419-774-5501 and the treasurer's number is 419-774-5622.

A third body, the Richland County Board of Revision, hears complaints about value. Its three statutory members are the auditor, the treasurer and the chair of the board of county commissioners, and each can appoint a stand-in. For a seller the split is easy to remember. Questions about value, exemptions and complaints go to the auditor. Questions about what is owed, payment contracts and delinquency go to the treasurer.

  • Auditor, 419-774-5501: valuation, Board of Revision complaint forms, owner occupancy and homestead applications, CAUV farmland.
  • Treasurer, 419-774-5622: bills, payments, payment contracts on real estate, and conveyance fee payments.
  • Sheriff's civil section, 419-774-3570: tax foreclosure and bank foreclosure sales.

sections.h2: What does the Richland County housing market look like on paper?
sections.html:
Richland County covers 495.23 square miles of land, with Mansfield as the county seat and the center of the Mansfield metropolitan area. The county was created in 1808 and organized in 1813, and Ashland County was cut out of its eastern side in 1846. It holds four cities (Mansfield, Ontario, Shelby and part of Galion), villages such as Bellville, Lexington and Shiloh, and 18 townships.

About two thirds of homes are owner occupied, and the 2020 census counted 66.3% of residents in urban areas. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts figures below show the scale of the local housing stock.

sections.h2: When does Richland County revalue property again?
sections.html:
The auditor's page says the county's triennial update falls in tax year 2026, with the resulting bills payable in 2027. Ohio reappraises on a six-year cycle and updates values at the three-year midpoint without a physical inspection.

The auditor also summarizes three state reforms enacted in late 2025. House Bill 186 creates an inflation cap credit that can apply in school districts sitting at the 20-mill floor, and any such credit must appear as its own line on the bill. House Bill 335 limits growth in inside millage during valuation reset years to the pace of inflation. House Bill 129 changes how the 20-mill floor is calculated, starting with tax year 2026. The auditor adds that these laws do not eliminate property taxes or freeze values.

sections.h2: How do I file a Board of Revision complaint in Richland County?
sections.html:
File the complaint form with the Richland County Auditor, 50 Park Avenue East in Mansfield. The county's Board of Revision page gives the filing period as January 2 through March 31 each year and says there is no filing fee. Section 5715.19 of the Revised Code states the cutoff as March 31 or the close of first-half collection, whichever is later, and treats a postmark on a mailed complaint as the filing date.

The county suggests calling the auditor before filing, because a flawed complaint can be dismissed. Keep these points in mind.

  • One complaint per parcel in a triennial period, unless the property sold, suffered a casualty or lost income. A complaint that was withdrawn still counts as the filing for that period.
  • Parcels can share a form only when they are contiguous or one economic unit, in the same taxing district, with identical ownership. When in doubt, file separately.
  • Attach the supporting documents you plan to use at the hearing when you file.
  • Notice of the hearing arrives by certified mail at least 10 days ahead, and the hearing is held in the auditor's office.

After the Board issues its written opinion of value, an owner who still disagrees can appeal to the State Board of Tax Appeals or to the common pleas court.

sections.h2: What evidence does the Richland County Board of Revision accept?
sections.html:
The burden of proof sits with the person who files. The Board may raise, lower or leave the value alone, and the county lists the kinds of proof it weighs: sales of similar properties, independent fee appraisals, itemized professional repair estimates, the closing statement and purchase contract if the home sold recently, and income and expense statements for rentals.

Two limits matter to sellers. Sheriff's sales, bank sales, short sales and any sale where buyer or seller faced unusual pressure are not treated as arm's length, so they do not count as comparables. The Board also has no power over the tax rate, the percentage increase in a bill, the CAUV formula or the dollar amount of a bill, so a complaint that only objects to a higher bill goes nowhere.

sections.h2: Which tax reductions can a Richland County homeowner claim?
sections.html:
The Ohio Department of Taxation describes three common programs, all handled through the county auditor. The owner occupancy credit applies to a home you own and live in as your primary residence on January 1 of the year you apply. The homestead exemption is for owners who are 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled, or certain surviving spouses, with an income test for most applicants and none for service-connected disabled veterans. Ohio House Bill 96 of 2025 also lets county commissioners adopt a local-option homestead exemption equal to the state amount, which applies without a separate application if the county turns it on. Ask the Richland County Auditor whether that local option is in place.

Farmland has its own track. Current agricultural use value, or CAUV, lets qualifying land be taxed on its farm value rather than market value. The state asks for ten or more acres in commercial agriculture, or less than ten acres with average yearly gross farm income of at least $2,500. The county's CAUV page says the formula averages seven years of data with the high and low years dropped.

A seller of farmland should know that section 319.202 requires the buyer's conveyance statement to say whether the land was in CAUV, and that land leaving the program can trigger a recoupment charge.

sections.h2: How are Richland County taxes paid, and what if I am behind?
sections.html:
The treasurer collects real estate, personal property, mobile home and estate taxes, and accepts online payment by card or eCheck with a service fee. Payment contracts are available on real estate for both prepayment and delinquent amounts. State law sets the base dates at December 31 and June 20 and lets counties extend them, so read the dates printed on your bill or ask the treasurer's office.

Under section 323.121 of the Revised Code, a missed installment draws a ten percent penalty, and if the full amount is paid within ten days after a due date, half of that penalty is waived. Interest then accrues on delinquent taxes. The treasurer's page states that the delinquent tax collector works with the county prosecutor on foreclosures, which is why an unpaid parcel can move from a bill to a court case.

Once a valid delinquent tax contract is in force, the statute stops further interest, and if the contract is breached the stopped interest and penalty are added back. A seller with a contract in place should ask the treasurer for a written payoff before the closing date.

sections.h2: What happens when a Richland County parcel reaches a tax foreclosure sale?
sections.html:
Tax foreclosure sales, when scheduled, are held on Friday mornings at 10:00 in the training room of the Sheriff's Office at 597 Park Avenue East in Mansfield. The sheriff advertises each parcel in a newspaper beginning three weeks before the first sale, reads withdrawals aloud at the start of the sale, and requires the winning bidder to pay in full at the sale. A parcel that draws no sufficient bid can be offered again two weeks later at the same minimum price.

Bank foreclosure sales follow a separate path. To comply with Ohio House Bill 390, they are conducted only online through the sheriff's auction site, and the sheriff recommends that first-time bidders finish the site's training well before an auction. The county Land Bank, at 50 Park Avenue East, lower level 1, works to acquire vacant and abandoned properties and return them to use.

An owner facing a tax judgment should call the treasurer's office at 419-774-5622 before the sale date to ask what payment, contract or sale the county will accept.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Richland County house when taxes are still owed?
sections.html:
Start with a written balance from the treasurer, then compare it with the auditor's parcel record so the legal description, owner name and tax mailing address agree. The conveyance statement filed with the auditor under section 319.202 must disclose whether the property carried a tax reduction or CAUV status, and the seller pays the conveyance fee plus any county transfer tax before the deed goes to the recorder.

Whatever sale route you choose, line up three things early: the treasurer's payoff, the auditor's conveyance paperwork, and tax map pre-approval for the deed at the recorder.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Richland County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Richland County Treasurer at 419-774-5622 about amounts owed, payments and contracts. Call the Auditor at 419-774-5501 about value, exemptions and Board of Revision complaints. Both offices are at 50 Park Avenue East in Mansfield.

faqs.q: What is the filing window for a Richland County valuation complaint?
faqs.a: The county's Board of Revision page lists January 2 through March 31 each year, filed with the auditor at no charge. State law allows a later date if the first-half collection closes after March 31.

faqs.q: Does Richland County have a tax revaluation in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. The county auditor says the triennial update occurs in tax year 2026, with taxes payable in 2027. State changes from House Bills 186, 335 and 129 are tied to those reset years.

faqs.q: Can I stop a Richland County tax foreclosure sale by selling the house?
faqs.a: Possibly, but ask first. Call the treasurer at 419-774-5622 for the judgment payoff and confirm timing with the sheriff's civil section at 419-774-3570.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed after selling in Richland County?
faqs.a: File it with the Richland County Recorder at 50 Park Avenue East in Mansfield. The recorder accepts deed transfers electronically but asks that tax map pre-approval be included. Documents that need tax map and auditor review must be brought to the courthouse in person.
